release_context.label: Latest monthly labor-market releases available as of November 6, 2026
release_context.note: Values are public, seasonally adjusted headline indicators from BLS series as displayed by FRED. Data may be revised.

indicators.label: Unemployment rate
indicators.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.interpretation: Headline unemployment fell to 4.1, keeping the labor market tighter.

indicators.label: Labor force participation
indicators.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.interpretation: Participation rose to 61.9, improving worker availability.

indicators.label: Total nonfarm payrolls
indicators.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.interpretation: Payroll employment increased by 165 thousand to 159,293, a positive hiring signal.

indicators.label: Job openings
indicators.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.interpretation: Openings rose by 333 thousand to 7,523, a labor-demand signal to compare with hiring and quits.

indicators.label: U-6 labor underutilization
indicators.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.interpretation: Broader labor underutilization rose to 7.9, capturing slack beyond the headline unemployment rate.

indicators.label: Production and nonsupervisory hourly earnings
indicators.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.interpretation: Hourly pay for production and nonsupervisory workers rose to $32.75, a worker-pay gauge to read alongside inflation and hours.

sources.name: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey
